### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every case ran A36, then exactly one of three alternative activities — A14 in about 35 in 100 cases, A15 in about 30, A20 in about 35, never two of them together — and each of the three was always followed by A21, so A21 came two steps after A36 in every case. In the later window, A14, A15 and A20 are not observed in any of the 200 traces, A36's observed outgoing transitions all go to A21, and A21 immediately follows A36 (one step) in every case. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, REL001, REL002, REL005]
- The pairwise relations match this picture: before, A21 co-occurred with A14, A15 or A20 in about 35, 30 and 35 in 100 cases respectively and always came after them, and A36 preceded each of the three in the same shares; in the later window A21 appears without any of the three in all cases. [REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]
- Event positions shifted slightly, consistent with the missing step: A36 now sits a little later in the trace (mean relative position about 0.32 vs 0.33) and A21 a little earlier (about 0.39 vs 0.37); these are sequence positions, not clock times. [POS004, POS005]
- Out of A19, the share of observed outgoing transitions to A26 rose from about 41% to about 60%, while the shares to A16 (about 31% to 16%) and A17 (about 28% to 23%) fell; all three successors remain in use (97 vs 111 outgoing transitions behind the profiles). [DIR003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the three-way choice between A14, A15 and A20, which in the earlier window sat between A36 and A21, is no longer executed in the later window, so that A36 leads directly to A21 and this group of activities is bypassed. This rests on direct relational evidence: A36's successor profile changed from a roughly 35/30/35 split across A20, A15 and A14 to A21 alone, the A36-to-A21 distance shrank from two steps to one in all 200 traces, and participation in A14, A15 and A20 fell from about 30–35 in 100 cases to zero, where previously each of the three had always led to A21. The control-flow family produced 23 qualifying items against roughly 0.37 expected for an unchanged process, so chance sampling cannot account for the pattern as a whole, and the occurrence, direction, relation and lag indicators all describe the same structure consistently. A limitation remains: zero participation strictly means only that A14, A15 and A20 were not observed in the later sample, so a very rare continued execution of them cannot be fully excluded, although the all-case lag and successor evidence makes any frequent persistence implausible. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, REL003, REL006, REL008]

Other differences: the routing out of A19 shifted towards A26 at the expense of A16 and A17, with all three successors still observed in both windows; this is a share shift among existing paths and is separate from the main hypothesis above. [DIR003]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Setup:
- 200 traces before, 200 traces after.
- Screening: 94 units tested, 0.38 items expected without change overall. By family: control_flow: 74 units tested, 23 items, 0.37 expected without change. Time: 20 units tested, 0 items, 0.01 expected.

So control flow family: 23 items vs 0.37 expected — that's many times larger (about 60x). This cannot be explained by chance as a whole. So we're past the screening comparison; we judge by directness, consistency, and ruling out competing explanations.

Evidence items (all control flow, no time or resource items — so do not discuss time or resources):

OCC001: A14 — before: mean occurrences per trace 0.35, participation 0.35 (70/200 traces); after: 0.0, 0 traces. Decreased to zero.

OCC002: A15 — before 0.3 (60/200); after 0.0.

OCC003: A20 — before 0.35 (70/200); after 0.0.

DIR001: A14 — before outgoing transitions: A21 1.0 (all observed outgoing transitions of A14 go to A21); after: empty profile (A14 not observed). Support before 70, after 0.

DIR002: A15 — before: A21 1.0; after: empty. Support 60 → 0.

DIR003: A19 — before: A26 0.41, A16 0.31, A17 0.28; after: A26 0.60, A16 0.16, A17 0.23. Support 97 → 111. Redistribution of outgoing shares.

DIR004: A20 — before: A21 1.0; after: empty. Support 70 → 0.

DIR005: A36 — before: A20 0.35, A15 0.30, A14 0.35; after: A21 1.0. Support 200 → 200. So in the earlier window, A36 was followed by A20 (35%), A15 (30%), A14 (35%) of its observed outgoing transitions; in the later window, A36 is always followed by A21.

POS001-003: A14, A15, A20 — position support drops to 0 (not observed in later window). Before, they occurred around position ~0.35 of the trace (i.e., about a third of the way through).

POS004: A21 — support 1.0 in both; mean position shifted from ~0.387 to ~0.369 (slightly earlier). Small change.

POS005: A36 — support 1.0 in both; mean position shifted from ~0.316 to ~0.333 (slightly later). Small change.

REL001: A14/A15 — before: A_only 0.35, B_only 0.30, neither 0.35 (they never co-occur; they're alternatives); after: neither 1.0 (neither observed).

REL002: A14/A20 — before: A_only 0.35, B_only 0.35, neither 0.30; after: neither 1.0.

REL003: A14/A21 — before: cooccurrence 0.35 (A14 always with A21, A21 also alone 0.65); A_before_B 0.35; after: B_only 1.0 (A21 always, A14 never).

REL004: A14/A36 — before: cooccurrence 0.35, B_only 0.65, B_before_A 0.35; after: B_only 1.0.

REL005: A15/A20 — before: A_only 0.30, B_only 0.35, neither 0.35; after: neither 1.0.

REL006: A15/A21 — before: cooccurrence 0.30, B_only 0.70, A_before_B 0.30; after: B_only 1.0.

REL007: A15/A36 — before: cooccurrence 0.30, B_only 0.70, B_before_A 0.30; after: B_only 1.0.

REL008: A20/A21 — before: cooccurrence 0.35, B_only 0.65, A_before_B 0.35; after: B_only 1.0.

REL009: A20/A36 — before: cooccurrence 0.35, B_only 0.65, B_before_A 0.35; after: B_only 1.0.

LAG001: A36→A21 — before: lag 2 (A21 two steps after A36); after: lag 1 (immediately next). Support 200/200 both.

Now let me reconstruct the behaviour:

Before window:
- A36 occurs in all traces (support 200/200), at mean relative position ~0.32.
- After A36, the next activity is A14 (35%), A15 (30%), or A20 (35%) — three alternatives.
- Whichever of A14/A15/A20 occurs, it is followed by A21 (DIR001/002/004: 1.0 to A21).
- A21 occurs in all traces (POS004 support 1.0), at mean relative position ~0.39.
- A14/A15/A20 never co-occur (REL001/002/005: cooccurrence 0.0), each appears alone in its share of traces — they are alternatives (a choice of one of three).
- A14/A15/A20 co-occur with A21 in 0.35/0.30/0.35 of traces, and A21 alone in the rest — wait, that's odd. If A14 is followed by A21 in every trace where A14 occurs, then A14 and A21 co-occur in every trace containing A14. Cooccurrence 0.35 = participation of A14. And B_only (A21 without A14) 0.65. Yes consistent: A21 occurs in all traces; A14 in 35%; so cooccurrence 0.35, B_only 0.65.
- A_before_B 0.35 for (A14, A21): A14 comes before A21 in the 35% of traces with A14. Consistent with A36 → A14 → A21.
- For (A14, A36): cooccurrence 0.35, B_before_A 0.35 (A36 before A14). Consistent with A36 → A14.
- LAG001: A36 → A21 with lag 2 in all traces before: A36 at position p, A21 at p+2, with one of A14/A15/A20 in between.

After window:
- A14, A15, A20 are not observed at all (0 traces).
- A36 occurs in all traces, followed always by A21 (DIR005 after: A21 1.0).
- LAG001: A36 → A21 with lag 1 (immediately consecutive) in all traces.
- A21 occurs in all traces, slightly earlier relative position (~0.37 vs ~0.39).
- A36 slightly later (~0.33 vs ~0.32).

So the change: the block of three alternative activities A14/A15/A20 between A36 and A21 disappeared. In the earlier window, A36 was followed by exactly one of A14, A15, A20 (chosen per case, roughly 35/30/35 split), and that activity was followed by A21. In the later window, A36 is directly followed by A21; A14, A15, A20 are no longer observed.

This is a bypass/removal: a group of activities (the three alternatives) is skipped; A36 now leads directly to A21. Per the instructions: "It does not apply when an activity or path is (nearly) absent in one window, when a predecessor now leads directly to a successor so that a group of activities is bypassed" — so this is NOT a "change in how often existing paths are taken" hypothesis; it's activities removed/bypassed (became skipped/optional→absent).

Hypothesis: A14, A15, A20 were removed from the process (or the path through them was removed), so that A36 now leads directly to A21. This is supported directly by:
- OCC001-003: participation 35/30/35 in 100 → 0.
- DIR005: A36's outgoing transitions changed from split across A20/A15/A14 to always A21.
- DIR001/002/004: A14/A15/A20 always led to A21 before; now unobserved.
- LAG001: A36→A21 distance changed from 2 steps to 1 step — direct relational evidence that A36 now leads directly to A21.
- REL003/004/006/007/008/009: co-occurrence of each of A14/A15/A20 with A21 and A36 dropped to zero; A21-only became 1.0.
- POS004/005: A21 slightly earlier, A36 slightly later — consistent with removing one step between them (positions are relative, so with a shorter trace the relative positions shift slightly).

Competing explanations: Could A14/A15/A20 still exist but not be observed? Zero participation only means not observed in that window. But with 200 traces and consistent relational evidence (LAG change from 2 to 1 in all 200 traces), the evidence is strong. Could this be a rare variant thing? No — these activities had 30-35% participation before (60-70 traces each), substantial.

Is the hypothesis "Supported" or "Weak"? The screening comparison: control flow family 23 items vs 0.37 expected — many times larger, so chance as a whole can't explain it. The evidence is direct (OCC + DIR + LAG + REL all consistent), consistent across many items, and rules out competing explanations well: the LAG change from lag 2 to lag 1 in all traces directly shows A36 now immediately precedes A21; the DIR change shows A36's successor changed. The alternative explanation "the three activities still occur but weren't sampled" is weak given 200 traces and 30-35% prior participation — that would be extremely unlikely. Also, could it be that the three activities were replaced by something else between A36 and A21? LAG shows lag 1, so nothing sits between them (within five steps window; lag 1 means adjacent). So the bypass is direct.

I'd say "Supported hypothesis": the evidence supports directly and consistently that the alternative block A14/A15/A20 between A36 and A21 is no longer executed; A36 leads directly to A21.

One caution: zero participation only means not observed. But the combination (DIR005 showing A36→A21 always, LAG001 showing lag 1 always in 200/200 traces) directly shows the new behaviour, not just absence. So the positive evidence for the new structure is direct.

DIR003 (A19's outgoing shares redistributed: A26 up from ~41 to ~60 in 100, A16 down from ~31 to ~16, A17 down from ~28 to ~23) — this is a separate difference, a shift in routing shares out of A19. Support 97 → 111, both substantial. This is a secondary difference; report under "Other differences". Note: is this a "change in how often existing paths are taken"? A19 is observed in ~97/200 and ~111/200 traces (support = outgoing transitions of A19... actually support for DIR is outgoing transitions of the source activity). All successors (A26, A16, A17) observed in both windows. So it's a shift in shares between existing alternatives. But it's not part of the main hypothesis. Report as other difference.

POS004/POS005: small position shifts of A21 (earlier) and A36 (later) — these are consistent with the main change (removing one step between them shortens the trace segment; relative positions shift). Actually, wait — if an activity is removed, the total trace length decreases, so relative positions of remaining activities change. A36 at ~0.32→0.33 (later), A21 at ~0.39→0.37 (earlier). Hmm, A36 later and A21 earlier — they converge, consistent with the gap between them shrinking from 2 steps to 1. These are part of the main change's signature, though POS uses positions not clock time. I can mention them as consistent with the convergence of A36 and A21.

Actually, let me be careful: POS005 direction "increased" (A36 later), POS004 "redistributed" with mean decreased (A21 earlier). Both small (~0.017-0.019 in relative position units). These are minor; I can mention briefly or fold into the main description.

Now, the main hypothesis: "A choice block of three alternative activities (A14, A15, A20) between A36 and A21 was removed/bypassed: in the earlier window each case went A36 → one of A14/A15/A20 → A21; in the later window A36 is directly followed by A21 and the three activities are no longer observed."

Support level: Supported hypothesis. The evidence is direct (OCC, DIR, LAG, REL), consistent (many items describing one structure), and the screening count (23 vs 0.37 expected) rules out chance as a whole. Competing explanation that cannot be fully ruled out: the three activities might still be executed in a small share of cases not captured in the 200-trace sample (zero participation only means not observed) — though the all-traces LAG/DIR evidence makes any substantial persistence unlikely. Also cannot rule out that the three activities were replaced by a single merged activity elsewhere — but LAG 1 shows nothing between A36 and A21; the activities could theoretically have moved elsewhere in the process, but there's no evidence of them anywhere (participation 0). Hmm — "zero participation only means the activity was not observed in that window" — so strictly, they could have moved to a different part of the process rather than being removed. But with 0 occurrences in 200 traces each, and no evidence of them elsewhere, removal/not-executed is the parsimonious reading. I should mention the limitation: absence from the sample doesn't prove removal from the process; they might occur below the sampling rate.

Let me now quantify:

Before:
- A14 in about 35 in 100 traces (70/200), A15 about 30 in 100 (60/200), A20 about 35 in 100 (70/200). A_only 0.35 means A14 without A15; B_only 0.30 A15 without A14; neither 0.35 — neither of A14 nor A15, which would be traces with A20. Yes: exactly one of the three per trace.)
- A36 in all traces; its outgoing transitions: 35% to A20, 30% to A15, 35% to A14 (DIR005 before).
- A14/A15/A20's outgoing: always A21 (DIR001/002/004).

- A21 in all traces.

After:
- A14, A15, A20: 0 in 200 traces.
- A36 in all traces; outgoing: always A21 (DIR005 after).
- A36→A21: adjacent (1 step) in all traces (LAG001 after).
- A21 in all traces, mean relative position ~0.37 vs ~0.39 before; A36 ~0.33 vs ~0.32 before.

Other differences:
- DIR003: out of A19, share going to A26 rose from about 41% to about 60% of observed outgoing transitions; to A16 fell from about 31% to about 16%; to A17 from about 28% to about 23%. Support 97 → 111 outgoing transitions. This is a redistribution among existing successors, all still observed.
- POS004/POS005 small shifts — I'll fold into main description rather than "other", since they're part of the same behaviour (positions converge). Actually they could be listed as consistent with the main hypothesis.

Screening comparison: control_flow family: 23 items vs 0.37 expected — many times larger (roughly 60×). Time family: 0 items vs 0.01 expected — nothing. So the count comparison passes decisively; then judge directness/consistency.

Note: all items have empirical_strength 0.995 — that's because the differences are large/structural; but per instructions, high empirical strength alone doesn't separate real change from rare variant; the screening count and directness do.

Also note: 23 items but many reflect the same underlying behaviour (OCC/DIR/POS/REL for A14/A15/A20 are correlated — same traces). The instructions say agreeing items are not independent confirmations, and "do not merge items for this comparison" (the screening count comparison). For the qualitative judgement, consistency across indicator types (occurrence, direction, lag, relation) is what matters.

Hypothesis phrasing: "In the later window, the alternative step between A36 and A21 — one of A14, A15 or A20 chosen per case — is no longer executed; A36 leads directly to A21." This is a removal/bypass of a group of activities. Per the guidance, this is not a "path frequency shift" (that condition explicitly excludes bypass). It's "activities were removed / a group is bypassed". The hypothesis: part of the process (the three-way choice A14/A15/A20) is skipped / no longer executed.

Support level: Supported hypothesis. Direct evidence: DIR005 (A36's successor changed from the three alternatives to always A21), LAG001 (gap 2→1 in all traces), OCC001-003 (participation 30-35% → 0), DIR001/002/004 (the three always led to A21 before), REL003-009 (co-occurrence with A21/A36 dropped to zero). Consistent, direct, and the competing explanation (sampling fluctuation) is addressed by the screening count; the remaining competing explanation (activities still executed but unobserved in this sample) is unlikely but cannot be fully excluded — mention it.

Actually, should I consider "Weak" instead? The judgement criteria: "Supported hypothesis: the evidence supports a specific hypothesis directly and consistently." Here we have direct relational evidence (LAG, DIR) showing the new structure positively, not just absence. The change is large (30-35% participation → 0 across 200 traces; successor distribution 1.0 change). The screening count is ~60× expectation. I think "Supported hypothesis" is right, stated as a possibility supported by evidence, with the limitation that zero participation strictly means "not observed".
